proof: For n≥3, write N=n−2 and ρ=π/n. Fix the parity-selected type via the sum branch for odd numbers of pieces and the difference branch for even, with terminal interior angle π−β. For an admissible α′=ℓρ+εα including boundary rays, and even ℓ required for even n, a first-vertex trajectory exists and its type is εk−ℓ modulo N.

The labelled double polygon has one cone for odd n and two synchronized cones for even n. Matching forward and backward germ labels gives endpoint difference b−a equal to the adopted type. Affine angular lifts add a common label shift. In the even case hyperelliptic centrality synchronizes the shifts across the actual double, avoiding reliance on an unproved lift from the quotient.

The equal-modulus strip cylinders give a global affine shear on the double. Sector rotations and strict Euclidean length decrease imply reduction to model directions by CAT(0) properness and finiteness of saddle connections below a fixed length. In a model direction every germ reaches the reflected vertex, sides included. Transport gives b=C−a, all-germ first-vertex existence and the signed law without division by 2 in an even modulus. Triangle and square are independently handled.

The unrestricted angle-only type-zero criterion fails on direct diagonals for n≥5, including a self-fixed ray for (ℓ,ε)=(2,−1). This is outside the odd generic open sector and at the edge of the even one. The note is an adopted reading and credited rederivation, not an author erratum or a novelty claim.
